sections.title: Sound of the letter
paragraphs: The letter is named (i grec) /i ɡʁɛk/. It usually sounds like (yeux) /jø/, which means eyes. It makes two sounds in total.

sections.title: Pronouncing the letter
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the middle of your tongue high near the roof. Spread your lips wide and let the air flow smoothly. For the second sound, raise your tongue high and forward. Spread your lips firmly and hold the voice steady. Touch your throat to feel the voice buzz for both sounds.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: Before a vowel, the letter makes a gliding sound, as in (yoga) /jo.ɡa/. Between consonants, it sounds like a vowel, as in (cycle) /sikl/. At the end of a word, it also sounds like that same vowel, as in (jury) /ʒy.ʁi/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not let this vowel slide into a diphthong. In English, words like city often end in a relaxed sound. Keep your lips spread tight and your tongue high. Do not drop your tongue at the end.
